exam: What immediate step would you take for a newborn with vomiting and jaundice after starting breast milk? — Stop galactose exposure, start lactose‑free formula.
How does the presence of cataracts help differentiate galactosaemia from neonatal sepsis? — Cataracts are specific to galactitol accumulation, not seen in sepsis.
Which laboratory test is most specific for galactosaemia and what if it is unavailable? — Serum galactose‑1‑phosphate; if unavailable, use urine reducing substances plus clinical picture.
Why is vitamin K given to these infants? — Liver dysfunction can cause coagulopathy; vitamin K corrects deficiency while underlying cause is treated.
What long‑term complications should you monitor in a child with classic galactosaemia? — Liver fibrosis, cataracts, neurodevelopmental delay, and ovarian failure in females.

How would you distinguish classic galactosaemia from lactose intolerance in a toddler? — Classic presents with systemic toxicity and abnormal labs; lactose intolerance causes only GI symptoms without metabolic derangement.
Why is a low‑protein, galactose‑restricted diet preferred over a high‑protein diet in management? — Protein restriction is unnecessary; the key is removing galactose, not protein.
What are the contraindicated medications in galactosaemia and why? — None specific, but avoid drugs containing lactose as excipient because they add galactose.
ai.title: Galactosaemia
ai.subject: Biochemistry & genetics
ai.summary: Galactosaemia is an inherited defect in galactose metabolism causing accumulation of toxic metabolites. Early recognition and dietary restriction prevent liver, cataract and neurodevelopmental damage, especially in low‑resource settings.

b: Incidence: 1/30 000–1/60 000 live births worldwide; higher in some African populations.
Inheritance: autosomal recessive; both parents carriers.
sections.p: Galactosaemia results from autosomal recessive deficiency of galactose‑1‑phosphate uridyltransferase (GALT). It presents in newborns after milk feeding with jaundice, vomiting, and failure to thrive.

b: GALT transfers UDP‑glucose to galactose‑1‑phosphate, forming UDP‑galactose and glucose‑1‑phosphate.
sections.p: Normal pathway: dietary lactose → galactose → galactose‑1‑phosphate → UDP‑galactose via GALT. UDP‑galactose is used for glycoprotein and glycolipid synthesis.

b: No known up‑regulation; deficiency is absolute.
sections.p: GALT activity is constitutive; no major hormonal regulation. Enzyme activity is highest in liver, kidney and lens.

b: Cataracts from galactitol osmotic swelling of lens.
Developmental delay, seizures in severe cases.
sections.p: Loss of GALT leads to accumulation of galactose‑1‑phosphate, galactitol and galactonate, causing hepatic injury, cataract formation, and neurotoxicity.

b: Consider in any infant with unexplained jaundice, vomiting, or failure to thrive on breast/formula milk.
